experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages. Witness breathtaking panoramic views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. The trail offers diverse landscapes from subtropical jungle to alpine terrain, making it one of the world's most rewarding trekking experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges as clouds drift below you. The relatively short but rewarding hike through the Ghorepani area is accessible for most fitness levels and offers unforgettable photography opportunities.
experiences.location: Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and stunning views without the crowds of the main Annapurna circuit. Trek through dense forests of oak and rhododendron, alpine meadows, and high ridgelines with close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). Encounter local Gurung and Magar communities and experience authentic mountain village life along this off-the-beaten-path route.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Natural Hot Springs Soak at Jhinu Danda
experiences.description: After days of strenuous trekking, rejuvenate tired muscles in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda beside the Modi Khola river. These geothermal pools are a beloved rest stop for trekkers on the Annapurna Base Camp route. Soak in mineral-rich waters while surrounded by lush river valley scenery and listen to the rushing river below — a perfect blend of nature therapy and relaxation.
experiences.location: Jhinu Danda, Modi Khola Valley, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk & Dal Bhat Experience
experiences.description: Take a guided cultural walk through traditional Gurung villages such as Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung settlements in Nepal. Visit the Gurung Museum to learn about indigenous customs, traditional dress, and shamanic practices. End the experience with an authentic dal bhat meal — the staple trekker's feast of lentil soup, rice, vegetable curry, and pickles — prepared by a local family, offering genuine insight into mountain community life and cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 - clear immigration and collect baggage
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget taxi or shared bus from the airport to Thamel (Kathmandu's backpacker hub). Check into a budget guesthouse for one night. Visit a local gear shop to rent or buy any missing trekking equipment. Exchange currency at a local money changer for better rates.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's lively streets. Visit a local restaurant for a classic dal bhat dinner. Pick up snacks and supplies for the trek ahead. Rest early to prepare for an early morning bus.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick meal at a local Thamel eatery - try momos (dumplings) for around 200-300 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat (lentil soup, rice, vegetables) at a local Thamel restaurant for 400-600 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Book a tourist bus ticket to Pokhara for the next morning (around 800-1000 NPR). Keep all important documents accessible. Avoid expensive tourist restaurants in Thamel - look for places with locals eating.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Kathmandu to Pokhara by tourist bus (departs around 07:00, 6-7 hour journey). Enjoy scenic mountain views along the Prithvi Highway. Pack light snacks for the ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 13:00-14:00. Check into a budget guesthouse in Lakeside area. Visit the ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Project) office to obtain your ACAP permit (3,000 NPR for SAARC nationals, 3,000 NPR for others) and TIMS card (2,000 NPR). Organize gear and repack your bag for the trek.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Phewa Lake's Lakeside promenade. Enjoy views of the Annapurna range reflected in the lake at sunset. Have dinner at a local Lakeside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the bus departure - bread and tea at a local shop for 150-200 NPR
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside dal bhat during a bus stop for 300-400 NPR
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal at a local Pokhara restaurant for 500-700 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Permits are mandatory - ACAP and TIMS cards must be obtained before entering the trek. Carry passport-sized photos (2) for permit applications. Confirm your guesthouse in Pokhara has luggage storage if you plan to leave non-trekking items behind.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning local bus or jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (about 1.5-2 hours, 300-400 NPR). Begin the trek from Nayapul, crossing the Modi Khola river. Trek through terraced fields and small villages to Tikhedhunga (1,540m, approximately 3-4 hours of walking).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m). This is a steep but rewarding climb of about 3,280 stone steps. Enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding hills and valleys. Rest at a teahouse in Ulleri.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ulleri teahouse accommodation. Rest tired legs and enjoy the mountain village atmosphere. Socialize with fellow trekkers over tea.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs and toast at your Pokhara guesthouse for 300-400 NPR
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga for 400-500 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat dinner at your Ulleri teahouse for 500-600 NPR (often included or discounted with room)

day_by_day.notes: Teahouse accommodation in Ulleri costs approximately 300-500 NPR per night for a basic double room. Always drink boiled or filtered water (buy iodine tablets or use a filter bottle to save money). Carry a headlamp as teahouses have limited electricity.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for sunrise views over the hills. Trek from Ulleri through rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m). This is a moderate 3-4 hour hike with beautiful forest scenery. Check in at a teahouse in Ghorepani.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and acclimatize in Ghorepani. Explore the small village and interact with local Magar community members. Visit the local monastery if open. Prepare gear for the early morning Poon Hill hike.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy stunning sunset views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli from the Ghorepani ridge. Have dinner at your teahouse and plan the next day's early start.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse for 300-400 NPR
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread or noodle soup at a teahouse along the trail for 400-500 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Ghorepani teahouse for 500-700 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani has multiple teahouses - negotiate room rates as competition is high. Set an alarm for 04:30 for the Poon Hill sunrise hike next morning. October is peak trekking season so teahouses may be busy - arrive early to secure a room.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:30 and hike 45 minutes to Poon Hill (3,210m) for the most spectacular sunrise panorama of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Watch the golden light paint the Himalayan peaks including Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Dhaulagiri. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani through dense rhododendron forest to Tadapani (2,630m), approximately 4-5 hours. The trail offers continued mountain views and diverse forest wildlife including Himalayan birds.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani teahouse. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre from the village. Rest and recover from the long day.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea before Poon Hill hike, then full breakfast of eggs and toast on return for 350-450 NPR
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks on the trail, or stop at a small teahouse for noodle soup for 400-500 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse for 500-600 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is 50 NPR per person. Bring a warm jacket as it is very cold before sunrise at 3,210m. The Ghorepani to Tadapani trail can be muddy - use trekking poles if available. October weather should be clear and ideal for mountain views.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk around Tadapani to spot Himalayan birds (Danphe pheasant, Nepal's national bird, is commonly seen here). Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m), approximately 4-5 hours through forests and terraced farmland with spectacular Annapurna South views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong, a beautiful Gurung village. Explore the village, visit the ACAP checkpoint (mandatory permit check), and admire the iconic stone-paved streets. Chhomrong offers the last reliable mobile network before the sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from Chhomrong. Call family or friends as this may be the last good connectivity point. Rest and prepare for the deeper trek into the sanctuary.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Tadapani teahouse for 300-400 NPR
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried rice at a teahouse along the trail for 450-550 NPR
meals.dinner: Gurung bread with local honey or dal bhat at Chhomrong teahouse for 500-700 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is a key village - stock up on snacks (chocolate, energy bars, nuts) as prices increase significantly higher up the trail. Charge all electronic devices here as reliable power becomes scarce. Inform someone of your trekking plans.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down a long stone staircase to Sinuwa (2,360m), then continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m). The trail enters the Annapurna Conservation Area's inner zone. Approximately 3-4 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery to Dovan (2,600m). The Modi Khola river roars below as the valley narrows. Spot waterfalls cascading down steep cliffs. Arrive at Dovan teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Dovan. The deep gorge creates an atmospheric evening setting. Listen to the sound of the river and enjoy the remote mountain environment. Prepare for higher altitude trekking tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and chapati at Chhomrong teahouse for 350-450 NPR
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at Bamboo teahouse for 500-600 NPR (prices rise from here)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Dovan teahouse for 600-700 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Prices increase significantly inside the sanctuary - budget 600-900 NPR per meal from this point. Teahouse accommodation is basic (shared bathrooms, thin walls) but adequate. Carry water purification as clean water sources are available along the trail. Watch for leeches on the trail in forested sections.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan through the narrow gorge to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m), approximately 2 hours. Continue to Hinku Cave (3,170m) where trekkers historically sheltered. Arrive at Deurali (3,230m), the last stop before the sanctuary opens up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest at Deurali and acclimatize. The altitude is becoming significant - take it slow. Walk short distances around the teahouse area. The gorge walls tower above and the environment becomes more alpine. Watch for mountain goats on the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at Deurali teahouse. The night sky at this altitude is spectacular if skies are clear - look for stars and the Milky Way. Eat a hearty dinner and rest well for the final push to Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with dried fruit and tea at Dovan for 400-500 NPR
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (helps with altitude) and bread at Himalaya Hotel for 500-650 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Deurali teahouse for 650-800 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a traditional Nepali remedy for altitude sickness - highly recommended from this elevation. Watch for signs of altitude sickness: headache, nausea, dizziness. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Deurali can be cold and windy - layer up. The trail from Dovan to Deurali can have avalanche risk - check with teahouse owners.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Deurali (06:00-07:00) to reach Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) before midday. The trail emerges from the gorge into the stunning open amphitheater of the Annapurna Sanctuary. Views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) are breathtaking. Approximately 2-3 hours from Deurali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m), approximately 2 more hours. Arrive at the iconic ABC surrounded by a 360-degree panorama of Himalayan giants: Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. Check into your boutique stay accommodation at Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the spectacular alpenglow on the surrounding peaks as the sun sets. The peaks glow orange, then pink, then purple in a magical display. Take photographs and absorb one of the world's most dramatic mountain environments.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Deurali for 400-500 NPR - eat well before the climb
meals.lunch: Hot soup and snacks at MBC teahouse for 600-750 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at ABC accommodation for 700-900 NPR

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m is high altitude - move slowly and drink plenty of water. Headaches are common - rest and hydrate. The boutique stay at Annapurna Sanctuary offers slightly more comfortable accommodation than standard teahouses. Temperatures at ABC can drop to -10°C or below at night in October - use all available sleeping bag layers. Mobile connectivity is very limited or nonexistent at ABC.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 05:30) to witness the golden sunrise on the Annapurna massif from ABC. The light show on the surrounding 7,000m and 8,000m peaks is one of the most spectacular sights in the Himalayas. Explore the base camp area and walk along the moraine for different viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring different viewpoints around ABC. Walk toward the glacier moraine for close-up views of the icefall and Annapurna I's south face. Visit the small memorial to mountaineers who lost their lives on the Annapurna peaks. Take time to reflect in this extraordinary natural cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at ABC. Enjoy another stunning sunset on the peaks. Share stories with fellow trekkers from around the world. Rest well as the descent begins tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and multiple cups of tea to warm up after the cold sunrise for 450-550 NPR
meals.lunch: Fried rice or noodles at ABC teahouse for 650-800 NPR
meals.dinner: Celebratory dal bhat dinner at the boutique stay for 700-900 NPR

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire 14-day journey - take time to fully appreciate the environment. Annapurna I (8,091m) has one of the highest fatality rates of any 8,000m peak - respect the mountain. Do not attempt to go beyond designated trekking areas. Stay hydrated and watch for altitude sickness symptoms. October should provide excellent clear views.

day_by_day.morning: Begin descent from ABC (4,130m) back to MBC and continue down to Deurali. The descent is faster but harder on the knees - use trekking poles. Enjoy the changing scenery as you descend back into the gorge. Approximately 4-5 hours to reach Bamboo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending through Himalaya Hotel and Dovan to reach Bamboo (2,310m). The lower altitude means easier breathing and warmer temperatures. The forest becomes denser and greener as you descend. Arrive at Bamboo teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Bamboo. Celebrate completing the ABC trek with fellow trekkers. The lower altitude makes for a more comfortable night's sleep. Enjoy the sounds of the forest.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at ABC - porridge and tea for 450-550 NPR
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Dovan teahouse for 600-700 NPR
meals.dinner: Noodle soup or dal bhat at Bamboo for 550-650 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Descending from high altitude is hard on the knees - take breaks and walk with bent knees to reduce impact. Knee pain is common on descent - consider using trekking poles. Pace yourself and do not rush. The trail can be slippery - wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back up to Chhomrong (2,170m) via Sinuwa, approximately 3-4 hours. The stone staircase up to Chhomrong is challenging on tired legs. Stop at the ACAP checkpoint. Enjoy your last views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from Chhomrong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,780m), approximately 1.5-2 hours. Jhinu Danda has natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river - a perfect reward for tired trekking muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda (small entry fee of 200-300 NPR). The hot spring pools overlooking the river gorge are one of the trek's great pleasures. Stay overnight at Jhinu Danda teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Bamboo for 400-500 NPR
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Chhomrong for 500-600 NPR
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Jhinu Danda teahouse for 500-600 NPR

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a beloved tradition for returning ABC trekkers - do not miss them. Bring a towel and flip flops. The springs are open early morning to evening. Jhinu Danda is a quieter, less visited stop - enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Charge devices if solar power is available.

day_by_day.morning: Morning soak in the hot springs one more time before breakfast. Trek from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul via Kimche and the Modi Khola valley, approximately 4-5 hours. The trail passes through terraced farmland and small Gurung villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (300-400 NPR, 1.5-2 hours). Check back into a Lakeside guesthouse. Take a long hot shower - the first proper one in over a week. Do laundry (many guesthouses offer laundry service for 100-150 NPR per kg).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek with a lakeside dinner. Enjoy a cold local Everest or Gorkha beer (200-250 NPR). Stroll along Phewa Lake and reflect on the incredible journey. Watch the Annapurna range glow in the evening light from Pokhara.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Jhinu Danda for 350-450 NPR
meals.lunch: Grab a quick meal at Nayapul before the bus for 350-450 NPR
meals.dinner: Celebration meal at a Lakeside restaurant - try buff steak or pizza for a treat, 600-900 NPR

day_by_day.notes: You have successfully completed the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek - a major achievement! Rest your body well tonight. If time permits, consider a sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake (500-700 NPR for a rowing boat rental). Book your bus ticket back to Kathmandu for tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning in Pokhara. Optional: visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna range - a short hike or taxi ride away. Take a final walk along the lake and browse local craft shops for budget souvenirs (Thanka paintings, prayer flags, yak wool items).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tourist bus back to Kathmandu (departs around 07:00-08:00, arriving 14:00-15:00) or a domestic flight if budget allows (30 minutes, around 8,000-12,000 NPR). If returning by bus, arrive in Kathmandu and transfer to Thamel. Spend final hours exploring Thamel's craft markets for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu at a local Thamel restaurant. Try a traditional Newari feast or classic Nepali thali set. Pack bags and prepare for departure. Reflect on 14 incredible days in the Himalayas.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Pokhara Lakeside guesthouse - eggs, toast, fruit, tea for 350-500 NPR
meals.lunch: Roadside dal bhat during bus stop or airport/flight snack for 300-500 NPR
meals.dinner: Traditional Nepali Thali or Newari set meal at a Thamel restaurant for 600-800 NPR

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for the full 14 days: Permits (ACAP + TIMS): ~5,000 NPR | Transport (buses + local): ~3,000-4,000 NPR | Accommodation (13 nights at teahouses/guesthouses): ~8,000-12,000 NPR | Food (all meals): ~25,000-35,000 NPR | Miscellaneous (hot springs, Poon Hill fee, water, snacks): ~5,000-8,000 NPR | TOTAL ESTIMATED BUDGET: approximately USD 400-500 for the full 14 days excluding international flights and gear.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your hotel in Kathmandu (Thamel area recommended as a base before heading to Annapurna region). Rest and freshen up. Take a short orientation walk around Thamel neighborhood to get acquainted with the city, browse trekking gear shops if needed, and pick up any last-minute supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's vibrant streets, visit a local handicraft market, and enjoy your first evening in Nepal. Attend a brief cultural orientation session at your guesthouse if available.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Quick meal at the airport or a local Nepali restaurant near Thamel — try Dal Bhat (lentil soup with rice) at a mid-range local eatery (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded Thamel restaurant such as OR2K or Utse Restaurant — try Thakali set meal or Tibetan momos (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a licensed money changer in Thamel. Purchase a Nepal SIM card for connectivity. Confirm your trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) can be arranged next morning. Rest well to acclimatize to the altitude (~1,400m in Kathmandu).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Pashupatinath Temple and Boudhanath Stupa — two of Kathmandu's most iconic spiritual sites. Witness morning rituals and soak in the cultural atmosphere. Arrange your Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and TIMS card at the Nepal Tourism Board office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private jeep or tourist bus to Pokhara (approximately 6–7 hours drive or 25-minute flight if budget allows). Arrive in Pokhara by late afternoon. Check into a lakeside guesthouse. Take a relaxing walk along Phewa Lake's shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside (Baidam) area, browse local shops, and enjoy views of the Annapurna range at dusk if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kathmandu — eggs, toast, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside dal bhat during the drive to Pokhara (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara — try Moondance Restaurant or Caffe Concerto for a mix of Nepali and continental cuisine (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the tourist bus in advance from Thamel bus park (~$10–15 USD). Alternatively, a domestic flight Kathmandu–Pokhara takes 25 minutes (~$80–100 USD) and saves considerable travel time. Pokhara sits at ~820m elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn for a sunrise excursion to Sarangkot Hill (1,592m) — one of the best viewpoints for panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Hire a taxi or walk up the trail (~1.5 hours). Watch the golden light illuminate the peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the International Mountain Museum to learn about Himalayan history, climbing expeditions, and local culture. Then visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) by boat across Phewa Lake for stunning valley and lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Final gear check and packing for the trek. Visit a trekking outfitter if any last items are needed. Relax by the lakeside.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before Sarangkot — tea and snacks at a hilltop tea house (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Lakeside café — try a Nepali thali or pasta at a mid-range spot (~$6–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pokhara's Lakeside — try Momos and Tibetan bread at a local Tibetan restaurant (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your transportation to the trek starting point (Nayapul or Phedi) for tomorrow morning. Hire a local guide or porter through a reputable agency in Pokhara if desired (~$20–30/day for guide, ~$15–20/day for porter). October is peak trekking season — trails will be busy but weather is generally excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Early taxi or local bus from Pokhara to Nayapul (1–1.5 hours, ~$5–10 USD). Begin the classic Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Trek from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (1,540m) through terraced farmland, rhododendron forests, and small villages. Distance: ~12 km, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking or arrive at Tikhedhunga and explore the village. Visit the local watermill and interact with Gurung and Magar community members. Rest your legs and enjoy the mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse in Tikhedhunga. Enjoy the peaceful Himalayan village atmosphere as the sun sets over the ridgelines.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Pokhara before departure — eggs, porridge, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a teahouse in Hile or along the trail (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Tikhedhunga — vegetable curry, rice, and soup (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Trek difficulty: Easy to Moderate. Carry at least 2 liters of water and water purification tablets. Apply sunscreen and wear layers. Your ACAP and TIMS permits will be checked at the checkpoint in Birethanti. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani (2,860m) — one of the most scenic and challenging days of the lower circuit. Climb the famous stone staircase through dense rhododendron and oak forests. Distance: ~11 km, 5–6 hours with significant elevation gain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani by early afternoon. Rest and acclimatize to the higher altitude. Explore the village and enjoy views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m) and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the village or a nearby viewpoint. The alpenglow on Dhaulagiri at sunset is spectacular. Warm up with ginger lemon honey tea.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Tikhedhunga — porridge, eggs, and Nepali tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop in Banthanti — noodle soup or dal bhat (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ghorepani — garlic soup (great for acclimatization), dal bhat or pasta (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a demanding day with ~1,300m elevation gain. Take it slow and steady. Altitude sickness can begin above 2,500m — watch for symptoms like headache, nausea, and dizziness. Ghorepani has multiple teahouses with comfortable rooms (~$5–15 USD/night). Garlic soup is a local remedy for altitude sickness.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up (4:30–5:00 AM) and hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — a 45-minute ascent. Witness one of the most celebrated sunrises in Nepal with a 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machapuchare (Fishtail), Dhaulagiri, and dozens more peaks. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) through stunning rhododendron forests — the largest rhododendron forest in Nepal. Distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. Enjoy excellent views of Machapuchare (6,993m) throughout the walk.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani. Rest and enjoy the quieter, less-crowded teahouse atmosphere. Stargazing opportunity on clear nights at this elevation.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast after Poon Hill return — pancakes, eggs, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch along the trail — fried rice or noodle soup (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Tadapani — dal bhat set with seasonal vegetables (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: ~300 NPR (~$2.50 USD). Bring a headlamp and warm layers for the pre-dawn hike — temperatures can drop below freezing. The rhododendron forests on the Ghorepani–Tadapani trail are especially magical in October light. Tadapani has fewer teahouses — arrive early to secure a room.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (2,170m) — a beautiful descent and re-ascent through forests and terraced fields with stunning Annapurna South and Machapuchare views. Distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong, the last major Gurung village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary. Explore the village, visit the local monastery, and enjoy the spectacular mountain panorama from the village viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on a teahouse terrace with views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. This is a great spot to reflect on the journey so far and prepare mentally for the ascent into the sanctuary.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Tadapani — muesli with warm milk and eggs (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a teahouse in Sinuwa or along the trail — vegetable fried rice (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Chomrong — try the local apple raksi (distilled spirit) as an aperitif, followed by dal bhat (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong is a key resupply and rest point. Stock up on snacks, chocolate, and bottled water here as prices increase significantly higher up the trail. The Chomrong Khola (river) crossing involves a long descent and re-ascent — take it steadily. Your ACAP permit will be checked again at the Chomrong checkpoint.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong to Dovan (2,600m) through bamboo and rhododendron forests. The trail descends to the Modi Khola river valley and follows it upstream into the increasingly dramatic gorge. Distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. Pass through Sinuwa and Bamboo teahouse stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Dovan. The gorge narrows dramatically here and the walls of the Annapurna Sanctuary begin to reveal themselves. Rest, explore the immediate surroundings, and listen to the rushing Modi Khola river.
day_by_day.evening: Cozy teahouse evening at Dovan. The forest atmosphere is magical — listen for wildlife in the surrounding jungle. Journal or read by candlelight.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Chomrong — porridge with honey and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Bamboo — noodle soup or dal bhat (~$6–8 USD, prices rise from here)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Dovan — pasta or vegetable curry with rice (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The trail from Chomrong into the sanctuary can be slippery after rain — trekking poles are highly recommended. The forest is dense and beautiful but can feel remote. This section is an avalanche zone in winter/spring — October is generally safe but be aware of your surroundings. Teahouse options at Dovan are limited — book ahead if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m), continuing through the spectacular Modi Khola gorge. The trail passes through Himalayan birch and rhododendron forest with increasingly dramatic cliff views. Distance: ~5 km, 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Himalaya Hotel to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — the crown jewel of the trek. As you pass through the Annapurna Sanctuary entrance (Machhapuchhre Base Camp at 3,700m), the landscape opens into a vast glacial amphitheater surrounded by 7,000m and 8,000m peaks. Distance from Himalaya Hotel to ABC: ~10 km, 4–5 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp — a truly awe-inspiring moment. You are surrounded on all sides by some of the world's highest mountains: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and Machapuchare. Watch the sunset paint the peaks in shades of gold and pink.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at Dovan — eggs and toast (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) — hot soup and bread (~$7–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at ABC — dal bhat or pasta (~$10–14 USD, prices are highest here)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Altitude sickness is a real concern — ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid alcohol. If you experience severe headache, vomiting, or difficulty breathing, descend immediately. October skies are typically clear, making for outstanding views. The teahouses at ABC are basic but adequate. Bring a warm sleeping bag — temperatures drop well below freezing at night.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp — arguably the most spectacular mountain sunrise experience in the world. The entire amphitheater of peaks glows in brilliant colors. Spend the morning exploring the sanctuary, walking around the glacier moraine, and taking in the extraordinary 360-degree mountain panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the descent from ABC back toward lower elevations. Trek from ABC down to Bamboo (2,310m) — a long but rewarding descent retracing the ascent route. Distance: ~15 km, 5–6 hours descent.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse. Celebrate completing the sanctuary portion of the trek. Enjoy the warmer temperatures and denser forest atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early morning tea and snacks at ABC before sunrise, then full breakfast after — porridge and eggs (~$6–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at MBC or Himalaya Hotel during descent — noodle soup (~$7–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Bamboo — dal bhat with extra helpings to replenish energy (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The descent is hard on the knees — use trekking poles and take breaks. The altitude drop from 4,130m to 2,310m in one day is significant and you may feel the pleasant effects of increased oxygen. Celebrate your achievement at ABC but don't rush the descent — many injuries happen on the way down. Bamboo is a welcome, lush, forested rest point.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo to Chomrong (2,170m), retracing the trail through the bamboo and rhododendron forests. Distance: ~8 km, 3–4 hours. Enjoy the forest scenery with fresh eyes on the descent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chomrong. Take a well-deserved rest. Visit the village monastery and interact with local Gurung families. Optional: take a short hike to a nearby viewpoint for a final look at Annapurna South and Machapuchare.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Chomrong — one of the most charming villages on the trail. Enjoy a hot shower (available at most teahouses for a small fee) and a proper sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at Bamboo — pancakes and tea (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch in Sinuwa — fried rice or pasta (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Chomrong — treat yourself to a slightly more varied menu: pizza, pasta, or a full Nepali thali (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong has better teahouse facilities than the higher camps — enjoy the relative comforts. This is a good day to air out gear, dry wet clothes, and reorganize your pack. Check in with your guide or porter and plan the next two days of descent. Many trekkers choose an alternate return route via Ghandruk — discuss options with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong to Ghandruk (1,940m) via the alternate return route — a beautiful trail through terraced fields and traditional Gurung villages with sweeping Annapurna views. Distance: ~8 km, 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk — one of the most picturesque and culturally rich villages in the Annapurna region. Visit the Gurung Museum to learn about the indigenous Gurung culture, traditions, and history. Walk through the stone-paved village lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cultural evening in Ghandruk. If lucky, witness traditional Gurung music and dance performances. The village has excellent teahouses with terraces overlooking Annapurna South and Machapuchare.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Chomrong — eggs, toast, and Nepali tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch along the trail or in Ghandruk — dal bhat (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ghandruk — try Gurung-style bread (Dhedo) with local vegetable curry (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk Museum entry fee: ~200 NPR (~$1.50 USD). Ghandruk is one of the most photographed villages in Nepal — the stone houses, terraced fields, and mountain backdrop are stunning. October light is particularly beautiful for photography. This village is also accessible by road from Pokhara, so you may see day visitors here.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the mountains — wake up early for last views of the Annapurna range from Ghandruk. Trek from Ghandruk to Nayapul (1,070m) — a pleasant descent through forests and villages. Distance: ~12 km, 4–5 hours. Take your time and savor the final hours on the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a jeep or taxi back to Pokhara (~1.5 hours, ~$5–10 USD). Check into a lakeside hotel in Pokhara. Enjoy a long hot shower and fresh clothes. Take a relaxing boat ride on Phewa Lake in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara to mark the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Explore the Lakeside area one more time.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Ghandruk — muesli, eggs, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Final trail lunch at a teahouse near Birethanti — dal bhat one last time (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a good Pokhara restaurant — Moondance, Caffe Concerto, or Beam Bar — try a multi-course meal with local craft beer or Everest beer (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Congratulations on completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek! Total trekking distance covered: approximately 110–120 km over 10 days. Tip your guide and porter generously — it is customary and greatly appreciated (~10–15% of their total fee). Visit a local pharmacy if you have any blisters or muscle soreness to address.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — optional sunrise visit to Sarangkot or a peaceful walk along Phewa Lake. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the lake (reach by rowboat). Browse the Lakeside market for last-minute souvenirs: Thangka paintings, singing bowls, pashmina scarves, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Pokhara back to Kathmandu (flight ~25 min or tourist bus ~6–7 hours). If time allows before departure, visit Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) in Kathmandu for panoramic city views and a final spiritual experience. Last-minute souvenir shopping in Thamel.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 14-day journey through one of the world's most magnificent mountain landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café breakfast in Pokhara — continental breakfast with fresh fruit juice (~$5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kathmandu Thamel area — final Nepali thali or a café meal (~$6–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner in Kathmandu before departure — Nepali or international cuisine (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Tribhuvan International Airport. Nepal's airport can be busy — arrive early. Declare any items of significant value at customs if required. Carry trekking permits and any receipts as mementos. Nepal departure tax is typically included in international airfare. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay in the Annapurna Conservation Area. En route, enjoy a scenic drive through the Prithvi Highway with views of terraced hillsides and the Trishuli River. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome orientation with your personal trek guide over afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique accommodation. Enjoy a curated welcome dinner on the terrace or in the lodge dining room, featuring traditional Nepali cuisine with a gourmet twist — dal bhat with organic local vegetables, slow-cooked lamb curry, and artisanal Himalayan cheese platter.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight
meals.lunch: Light snack box provided during private transfer
meals.dinner: Welcome gourmet Nepali dinner at the boutique lodge — dal bhat, lamb curry, seasonal vegetables, Himalayan cheese, and local raksi or premium wine

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) are confirmed prior to arrival. Your private guide will brief you on the 14-day plan. Hydrate well and rest early to acclimatize to the altitude. Pack layers for cool evening temperatures in October.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided nature walk around the lodge surroundings in the Annapurna Conservation Area. Observe endemic bird species including Himalayan monal and red-billed chough with a premium birding kit provided. Breathe in crisp mountain air and take in panoramic views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare (Fishtail Peak) at golden hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Acclimatization hike to a nearby viewpoint (2–3 hours, moderate pace). Your private guide leads you through rhododendron and oak forests, explaining local flora, fauna, and conservation efforts. Return to the lodge for a guided meditation and yoga session on the mountain-view deck led by a resident wellness instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural immersion evening — a local Gurung village elder visits the lodge for a private storytelling session about Annapurna mythology and mountain culture. Followed by a gourmet candlelit dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — Himalayan honey, freshly baked bread, local eggs, seasonal fruit, Nepali butter tea or French press coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch — whole grain wraps with grilled chicken, energy bars, fresh fruit, and thermos of herbal tea
meals.dinner: Candlelit gourmet dinner — Gurung-style pork ribs, buckwheat pancakes with wild honey, sautéed mountain greens, and premium imported wine

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day. Avoid overexertion. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. October brings clear skies and stunning visibility — ideal for photography. Bring a light down jacket for the morning walk.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the classic Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Depart lodge after breakfast on a guided trek toward Chhomrong (2,170m). The trail winds through terraced farmland, suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river, and lush subtropical forest. Your porter team carries all gear — you trek light with a premium daypack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong village by early afternoon. Check into a premium teahouse or pre-arranged luxury tented camp with private facilities. Explore Chhomrong village, visit the local monastery, and interact with Gurung families. Enjoy a private photography session with your guide capturing Annapurna South at sunset.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop dinner at the teahouse with unobstructed mountain views. Chef prepares a special multi-course meal with locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — eggs to order, granola, fresh juice, Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at a scenic rest point — smoked salmon wraps, trail mix, premium chocolate, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Multi-course teahouse dinner — pumpkin soup, grilled yak steak with herb butter, roasted potatoes, apple crumble with cream, and hot ginger lemon honey

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 5–6 hours. Elevation gain is moderate. Trekking poles recommended. Porter team is fully equipped. October weather is typically clear and dry — perfect trekking conditions. Ensure sleeping bag liner is accessible for cooler nights.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise viewing from Chhomrong ridge — spectacular alpenglow on Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. After breakfast, continue trek toward Sinuwa (2,360m) and Bamboo (2,310m) through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest. Listen for langur monkeys and observe rare Himalayan wildlife with your naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Dovan (2,600m). The trail becomes increasingly dramatic with waterfalls and towering cliffs. Arrive at Dovan teahouse by early afternoon. Rest and enjoy a private hot stone foot massage arranged by your luxury trek operator.
day_by_day.evening: Intimate dinner at the teahouse. Your private chef or teahouse cook prepares a customized menu. Stargazing session with a provided premium telescope — October skies in the Annapurna region are exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast — porridge with dried fruits and nuts, toast with Himalayan honey, boiled eggs, butter tea
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — energy bars, cheese and crackers, dried mango, nuts, and thermos of tomato soup
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner — vegetable thukpa (noodle soup), dal bhat with seasonal curries, momos (dumplings), and herbal mountain tea

day_by_day.notes: Today's combined trek is approximately 5–6 hours with some steep sections near Sinuwa. The bamboo forest can be slippery — trekking poles essential. Temperatures drop significantly at night at this elevation. Ensure down jacket and thermal layers are easily accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) through increasingly alpine terrain. The Modi Khola gorge narrows dramatically, with towering walls of rock and ice on either side. Your naturalist guide points out snow leopard tracks and Himalayan tahr on the cliffs above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hinku Cave (3,170m) and on to Deurali (3,230m). The landscape transforms into a high-altitude environment with sparse vegetation and dramatic glacial moraine. Arrive at Deurali and rest at a premium teahouse. Enjoy a private guided discussion on glacial geology and Himalayan ecology.
day_by_day.evening: Acclimatization evening at Deurali. Light stretching and breathing exercises led by your wellness guide. Early dinner and rest to prepare for the ascent to Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast — oatmeal with honey and walnuts, scrambled eggs, whole grain toast, Nepali milk tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Himalaya Hotel — hot noodle soup, tuna crackers, energy bars, dried apricots, hot lemon ginger tea
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner — garlic soup (altitude remedy), pasta with tomato sauce, steamed vegetables, chocolate brownie, herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Altitude is increasing significantly. Watch for early signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness). Your guide carries supplemental oxygen and a medical kit. Garlic soup is a traditional Nepali altitude remedy and is highly recommended. Drink plenty of fluids. Sleep with a thermal sleeping bag tonight.

day_by_day.morning: The iconic final ascent to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — the crown jewel of the trek. Depart Deurali at dawn for a 3–4 hour climb through the stunning Annapurna Sanctuary, a natural amphitheater ringed by some of the world's highest peaks: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machapuchare, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna. Arrive at ABC and take in the overwhelming panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided exploration of Annapurna Base Camp. Visit the mountaineering memorial and learn about historic Annapurna expeditions from your expert guide. Enjoy a celebratory Champagne toast at the rooftop of the ABC lodge — a premium experience arranged by your luxury operator. Photography session with a professional mountain photographer.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Annapurna Base Camp — one of the most spectacular sights in the Himalaya as the peaks turn gold and crimson. Special celebration dinner at the lodge with a curated menu and premium beverages.

meals.breakfast: Early power breakfast at Deurali — porridge, boiled eggs, toast, energy bars, hot tea
meals.lunch: Celebratory lunch at ABC — hot soup, sandwiches, chocolate cake, and a glass of sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Celebration gourmet dinner at ABC lodge — yak cheese fondue, roasted mountain vegetables, pasta primavera, imported wine, and a special dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Move slowly and breathe deeply. The Champagne toast is arranged in advance by your luxury operator — confirm with your guide. October provides the best visibility of the year at ABC. Professional mountain photographer accompanies the group for this day only — arrange in advance. Nights at ABC are extremely cold — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp — arguably the most breathtaking sunrise in Nepal as the first light illuminates the towering peaks above. Final photography session at ABC. Begin descent after breakfast, retracing the route back toward Deurali and Dovan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent to Bamboo (2,310m), enjoying the change in landscape as you descend through alpine meadows back into rhododendron and bamboo forest. The descent is faster but requires careful footing on rocky sections.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse by late afternoon. Enjoy a well-deserved hot shower (available at premium teahouses), a private massage session arranged by your luxury operator, and a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final ABC breakfast — eggs, toast, porridge, fresh fruit, hot tea and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Himalaya Hotel — hot soup, crackers, cheese, energy bars, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Bamboo — dal bhat, vegetable curry, lentil soup, fresh bread, and herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Descent is hard on the knees — trekking poles are essential. Take your time on steep sections. Your porter team handles all heavy gear. The transition from high altitude back to lower elevations brings warmer temperatures and richer oxygen — most trekkers feel noticeably better. Celebrate your ABC achievement with a small private toast this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo through Sinuwa back to Chhomrong (2,170m). The trail through the terraced fields and stone-paved paths of Chhomrong is a welcome return to village life. Visit the Chhomrong monastery for a private blessing ceremony arranged with the resident lama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village at leisure — visit local homes, interact with Gurung families, and learn about traditional weaving and farming practices. Enjoy a private cooking class with a local Gurung woman, learning to prepare traditional momos and dal bhat.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Chhomrong with your trekking crew — a tradition of gratitude and celebration. Tip ceremony for your guides and porters. Enjoy local Gurung dance and music performance arranged exclusively for your group.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast — pancakes with honey, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, butter tea
meals.lunch: Village lunch at a Chhomrong home — home-cooked dal bhat, fermented vegetables, and local chang (millet beer) or tea
meals.dinner: Celebratory crew dinner — momos, dal bhat, grilled chicken, local vegetables, raksi, and traditional desserts

day_by_day.notes: The private monastery blessing ceremony should be arranged 24 hours in advance through your luxury operator. The cooking class is a highlight of the cultural experience — participate fully. Tipping for guides and porters is customary and deeply appreciated — your operator will provide guidance on appropriate amounts.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chhomrong and trek back toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m), a beautiful riverside village known for its natural hot springs. The trail descends through terraced fields and suspension bridges over the Modi Khola.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jhinu Danda and enjoy a private session at the natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola — a deeply restorative experience after days of high-altitude trekking. Your luxury operator arranges a private hot spring session with premium towels, robes, and refreshments. Continue to Nayapul or Birethanti by private jeep.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury vehicle transfer to Pokhara (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check into a premium lakeside hotel or resort in Pokhara — such as Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or a comparable luxury property. Enjoy a relaxed lakeside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast — granola, yogurt, eggs, toast, fresh juice, coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Jhinu Danda hot springs — gourmet sandwiches, fruit, premium snacks, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Lakeside fine dining in Pokhara — grilled barramundi, Newari-style lamb, seasonal salad, imported wine, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a must — arrange the private session in advance. The transfer from Nayapul to Pokhara takes approximately 1.5–2 hours by private luxury jeep. Pokhara sits at 827m — the warmth and lower altitude will feel luxurious after days at high elevation. Enjoy a long, hot shower and a comfortable bed tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise flight over the Annapurna range from Pokhara — a 1-hour private mountain flight offering aerial views of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Machapuchare. Alternatively, sunrise viewing from Sarangkot Hill (private vehicle to the viewpoint at 4:30am). Return to hotel for a full luxury breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided boat ride on Phewa Lake in a private decorated wooden boat. Visit the iconic Tal Barahi Temple on an island in the middle of the lake. Explore the Pokhara lakeside area — browse high-end trekking boutiques, local art galleries, and Thangka painting studios. Private Thangka painting demonstration with a master artist.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel rooftop or a premium lakeside bar with Annapurna range views. Gourmet dinner at one of Pokhara's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast — buffet or à la carte, fresh juices, pastries, eggs to order, smoked salmon, Himalayan teas
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a premium restaurant — wood-fired pizza, fresh salads, grilled trout from Phewa Lake, and imported beer or wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a top Pokhara restaurant — Nepali tasting menu with amuse-bouche, heritage rice dishes, slow-cooked meats, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The mountain flight should be booked well in advance — October is peak season and flights fill quickly. Sarangkot sunrise is free but requires a 4:30am departure. The Thangka painting demonstration is a unique cultural experience — your luxury operator can arrange a private session with a renowned local artist. Pokhara is a great place to purchase high-quality souvenirs and trekking gear.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private guided excursion to the Annapurna foothills — visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) via a scenic hike with panoramic views of Phewa Lake and the Annapurna range. The hike takes approximately 45 minutes each way through forest trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — the most comprehensive mountaineering museum in Asia, featuring exhibits on all 14 eight-thousanders, Himalayan history, and indigenous mountain cultures. Private guided tour with a mountaineering historian. Followed by a visit to the Seti River Gorge — a stunning natural wonder where the Seti River disappears underground.
day_by_day.evening: Private cultural performance arranged at the hotel — traditional Gurung and Tharu dance and music. Followed by a curated Nepali fine dining experience at the hotel restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full buffet with fresh fruits, pastries, local specialties, and premium teas and coffees
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant near the museum — Newari set lunch, fresh salads, lassi, and dessert
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining — seven-course Nepali tasting menu featuring heritage recipes from across Nepal's ethnic communities, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: The World Peace Pagoda hike is gentle and suitable for post-trek legs. The International Mountain Museum is genuinely world-class — allow at least 2 hours. The private cultural performance should be arranged 48 hours in advance through your luxury operator. This is a wonderful day for journaling, photography, and reflection on the trek experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter excursion from Pokhara to Muktinath (3,800m) — a sacred Hindu and Buddhist pilgrimage site in the Mustang region, surrounded by dramatic high-altitude desert landscapes. The helicopter flight offers breathtaking views of the Kali Gandaki gorge and Dhaulagiri. Explore the ancient Muktinath Temple complex with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter return to Pokhara via a scenic route over the Annapurna Circuit. Alternatively, if weather conditions permit, a brief landing at a high-altitude meadow for a private picnic lunch. Return to Pokhara hotel by early afternoon. Enjoy a premium spa afternoon — full-body Ayurvedic massage, steam bath, and wellness treatments at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Private astrology reading by a traditional Nepali Jyotish (Vedic astrologer) arranged at the hotel. Farewell drinks on the terrace with Annapurna views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — power breakfast with eggs, avocado toast, granola, fresh juice, and coffee before the helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet high-altitude picnic lunch (helicopter excursion) — premium charcuterie, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Lakeside fine dining — fresh Phewa Lake trout, imported steak, seasonal vegetables, premium wine, and a special dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Muktinath helicopter excursion is weather-dependent — October is generally excellent but have a backup plan (extended spa day or Pokhara exploration). Book the helicopter well in advance through a reputable Pokhara-based operator. The Vedic astrology reading is a unique and memorable cultural experience — arrange through your luxury operator.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury vehicle transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu (approximately 6–7 hours via Prithvi Highway) or a 25-minute scenic mountain flight from Pokhara Airport to Kathmandu. Arrive in Kathmandu by midday. Check into a premium heritage hotel — such as Dwarika's Hotel or a comparable luxury property in the Thamel or Lazimpat area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Pashupatinath Temple (sacred Hindu site on the Bagmati River), Boudhanath Stupa (one of the largest stupas in the world), and Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple). Your expert guide provides deep cultural and historical context at each site.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Kathmandu's most acclaimed restaurants — Krishnarpan at Dwarika's Hotel or Bhojan Griha — featuring an elaborate Nepali royal banquet in a heritage setting with live classical Nepali music.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara hotel breakfast — full buffet before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch in Kathmandu upon arrival — Newari feast at a heritage restaurant near Boudhanath Stupa
meals.dinner: Royal Nepali banquet dinner — 22-course traditional Nepali royal cuisine at Krishnarpan (Dwarika's Hotel) or equivalent, with classical sarangi music performance

day_by_day.notes: The mountain flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu (25 minutes) is highly recommended over the road transfer for time efficiency and the spectacular aerial views. Book well in advance. Dwarika's Hotel is a UNESCO-recognized heritage property — a fitting luxury conclusion to the Nepal experience. Confirm the farewell dinner reservation at least 3 days in advance as Krishnarpan requires advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kathmandu — private guided shopping tour of Thamel and Asan Bazaar for premium Nepali souvenirs: hand-knotted carpets, singing bowls, Thangka paintings, pashmina shawls, yak wool products, and artisan jewelry. Your guide ensures authentic, fair-trade purchases. Visit a reputable pashmina showroom for premium cashmere and pashmina products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Garden of Dreams (Kaiser Garden) — a beautifully restored Edwardian-era neo-classical garden in the heart of Kathmandu. Enjoy a final farewell afternoon tea at the Kaiser Cafe within the garden. Private transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. Your luxury operator provides a full VIP airport assistance service — fast-track check-in, lounge access, and a farewell gift package.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kathmandu. Your farewell gift package includes premium Nepali tea, artisan chocolates, a hand-painted miniature Thangka, and a personalized trip memoir booklet prepared by your luxury operator.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — final luxury buffet with all favorites, fresh juices, pastries, and premium teas
meals.lunch: Farewell afternoon tea at Kaiser Cafe, Garden of Dreams — finger sandwiches, scones with clotted cream, petit fours, and premium Himalayan tea selection
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours before departure for Kathmandu airport check-in — the airport can be congested during peak October season. Your luxury operator's VIP airport assistance will streamline the process. Confirm excess baggage arrangements in advance if you have purchased significant souvenirs. The personalized trip memoir booklet is a premium touch — confirm this service with your operator at the start of the trip so they can compile photos and notes throughout the journey.
